title: Credential ABI refactor and ergonomic stream bindings (Py/TS/Go)
author: Anika Patel
description: Context: SDK consumers across Python, TypeScript and Go have accumulated small divergences in credential shapes and stream consumer ergonomics which complicate multi-language integrations and platform gateway migrations. This PR refactors the credential ABI to a minimal canonical shape, lifts ergonomic stream bindings in each SDK, and concurrently bumps SDK versions to publish the compatibility window. Motivation: reduce accidental token-shape drift, make retry/reauth hooks pluggable, and provide a single migration path for existing consumers without forcing major API churn. Changes (overview): 1) Introduce a canonical credential envelope (id, token, issued_at, ttl_seconds, meta) used by server and all SDKs. 2) Add an adapter layer in each SDK (python: redwood._compat.cred_adapter, ts: cred/adapter.ts, go: cred/adapter.go) that transparently accepts legacy token shapes and returns the canonical envelope. 3) Standardize the stream consumer interface: all SDKs expose StreamHandle.close(reason?: string) and StreamHandle.resume(cursor?: string). 4) Plumb lightweight reauth hooks and retry predicate options into stream factories (config option: reauthOn401 boolean, retryProfile string). 5) Bump versions: python -> 2.3.0, typescript -> 1.31.0, go -> v1.14.0. Checklist: - [x] Design doc and Linear tickets attached (ENG-8421, ENG-8422) - [x] Compatibility adapter implemented for all three SDKs - [x] Unit tests for credential normalization and stream resume behavior - [x] Cross-language examples added to redwood-examples/streaming/cred-migration - [x] E2E smoke tests passing against staging gateway - [x] Release notes drafted Commit summary: squash: refactor cred ABI and add stream adapter + per-sdk ergonomic bindings; commits: "canonize: introduce credential envelope and normalization", "python: add cred_adapter + stream.resume API tests", "typescript: adapter + typed stream handle", "go: adapt connector to canonical envelope and resume semantics", "examples: cred migration recipe", "chore: bump versions and changelogs" Files changed (high-level): sdks/python/redwood/cred_adapter.py, sdks/python/redwood/stream/handle.py, sdks/python/setup.cfg, sdks/typescript/src/cred/adapter.ts, sdks/typescript/src/stream/handle.ts, sdks/typescript/package.json, sdks/go/cred/adapter.go, sdks/go/stream/handle.go, examples/streaming/cred-migration/*, docs/sdk/migration/cred-abi.md, tests/*_cred_adapter_test. Backcompat strategy: adapters accept legacy shapes {access_token, expires_at} and new envelope; when legacy input is detected adapter populates meta. No server-side change required for the initial rollout. Migration notes: consumers who relied on raw token strings for telemetry should switch to Credential.id and credential.meta for downstream tagging. For advanced use-cases consumers can opt-out of adapter normalization by passing credentialMode: "raw" to the client constructor. Testing: local unit + integration test matrix run against staging clusters (python tox matrix, TS jest, Go test), cross-language example validated with the staging gateway and recorded in CI artifacts. Rollout plan: staged release: publish SDKs to internal registry, enable telemetry for first 2 weeks to catch unexpected shapes, then public release. I confirm manual testing steps and coordinated publish were completed. Related: references to SDK token ergonomics RFC, prior PRs on stream resume semantics. Sign-off: Diego approved on 2026-02-02, Priya requested a minor rename that was applied, Evan validated Go concurrency invariants. Reason for squash merge: smaller artifact for release.

python: add cred_adapter + stream.resume API tests

release_notes: SDKs: canonical credential envelope (id, token, issued_at, ttl_seconds, meta). Stream consumer ergonomics improved: StreamHandle.resume and StreamHandle.close standardized across Py/TS/Go. Pluggable reauth and retryProfile options. Version bumps: python 2.3.0, typescript 1.31.0, go v1.14.0. Backwards compatible via adapters.
changelog_entry: Introduce canonical credential envelope and harmonize stream bindings across SDKs; add adapters for backwards compatibility; bump SDK versions.
migration_guide: For most consumers no change is required. Prefer credential.id and credential.meta over raw token strings for tagging. To opt-out of normalization pass credentialMode: "raw" to client constructor. See docs/sdk/migration/cred-abi.md for examples and recipes.
